title: The Crooked Oath Again
premise: Lena Amberdale has spent her whole life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot enter, hiding the storm-calling blood she inherited from a mother she barely remembers. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley to seize her, Lena flees with a disgraced oath-keeper named Corren and discovers the truth: her mother was the last signatory of a covenant between the human realm and the storm-realm of Veyl, and that covenant is dying. To survive, Lena must gather the scattered heirs of the old oath-bearers — strangers who become the family she never had — and reforge the covenant at the Stormseat before the realms tear apart. In the end, Lena binds herself as the new living seal of the covenant, sacrificing her exile but gaining, at last, a place where she truly belongs.
about_author: Jude Galloway is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to maps of imaginary ones. They write stories about people who inherit more than they ever asked for.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet the Hollow, a valley where magic dies at the tree line, and Lena's quiet life mending roofs and hiding tremors in her hands when storms pass overhead. A traveling peddler mentions crown criers reading a proclamation: all gifted persons to be seized. Emotional beat: uneasy belonging — Lena loves the valley that has never quite loved her back.

chapters.title: Iron at the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Witch-hunters in grey iron cross into the Hollow — impossible, since magic cannot follow them here — led by the cold-eyed Inquisitor Vess. They carry a list of names, and Lena Amberdale is on it. Her foster father burns her mother's only letter rather than let it be found. Emotional beat: fear and betrayal as sanctuary becomes a trap.

chapters.title: What the Letter Burned
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with fragments of her mother's letter half-remembered from childhood. She learns her mother was an oath-bearer of Veyl, the storm-realm, and that the covenant binding it to the human world is failing. Hunted through the valley she knows better than her pursuers, Lena escapes over the ridge — past the line where magic begins again. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept a Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Beyond the valley, Lena is ambushed by hunters and saved by Corren, a disgraced oath-keeper whose own covenant-mark went dark years ago. He recognizes the storm-sign in her blood and grudgingly agrees to guide her toward the Stormseat. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people who have both been cast out.

chapters.title: The First Heir
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the river-city of Brassen, they find Maren, heir of the water-oath, who runs a ferry and wants nothing to do with realms or covenants. Vess's hunters arrive; Maren's gift floods the docks to cover their escape, and she leaves with them, furious and frightened. Emotional beat: the found family takes its first reluctant member.

chapters.title: Roads Full of Criers
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The crown's proclamation has turned every village against the gifted; neighbors denounce neighbors for a bounty. The three travelers pose as a merchant caravan, and small kindnesses from strangers remind Maren not everyone obeys the hunt. Emotional beat: the cost of hiding, and the first fragile trust within the group.

chapters.title: The Ash Choir
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the burned town of Cinderhollow they find Tam, a child who sings fire to sleep, orphaned by the hunt. Taking him is dangerous; leaving him is unthinkable. Corren teaches Lena the first words of the old covenant-liturgy, and her storm-blood answers for the first time outside the valley. Emotional beat: tenderness hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Vess's POV. We learn why she hunts: her sister was killed by a gifted mob years ago, and Vess believes the covenant itself is the rot. She interrogates a captured oath-heir and gains the location of the Stormseat road. Emotional beat: making the antagonist human without softening her threat.

chapters.title: The Mountain That Remembers
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. The company reaches the Oathspine mountains, where the stones still hum with covenant-memory. Corren confesses his failure: he was sworn to protect Lena's mother and arrived too late. Lena, furious, nearly abandons him — until Tam's nightmare-fire flares and only their combined gifts can quiet it. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Sky Gate
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At a ruined waystation, the heirs open a sliver of the sky-gate into Veyl and glimpse the storm-realm starving — its light dimming as the covenant fails. Something on the other side speaks Lena's name in her mother's voice. Emotional beat: wonder laced with dread; the stakes become cosmic, not just personal.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Cornered by hunters, Maren secretly offers Vess information in exchange for sparing Tam — then hates herself for it. Her betrayal lets Vess ambush the company at the ford. Corren is gravely wounded holding the crossing. Emotional beat: guilt, and the question of whether loyalty survives one bad night.

chapters.title: Salt and Ashes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Corren hovers near death; Lena, in desperation, calls a true storm for the first time — wild, terrifying, magnificent — to drive off the hunters. The display reveals her power to every spy on the road. Maren confesses her bargain; Lena cannot yet forgive her. Emotional beat: power embraced, trust broken.

chapters.title: The Hidden Court
chapters.summary: Tam's POV (limited, childlike). The fugitives shelter with the Veiled Court, an underground network of hidden gifted folk — bakers, midwives, soldiers — who have survived by concealment for generations. Their leader urges Lena to hide forever. Lena refuses: hiding is how the covenant died. Emotional beat: the pull of safety versus the call of duty.

chapters.title: Heir of the Deep Oath
chapters.summary: Corren's POV, recovering. The fourth heir is found in the unlikeliest place: Vess's own lieutenant, Sergeant Ilva, whose stone-oath bloodline has been serving the hunt unknowingly. Ilva defects with proof that Vess plans to destroy the Stormseat entirely, ending magic everywhere. Emotional beat: enemies discovering shared inheritance.

chapters.title: The March on the Stormseat
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided together. The five heirs travel openly now, gathering the Veiled Court behind them as an army of the hidden. Vess's forces shadow them, and the sky above darkens unnaturally — Veyl is dying faster than expected. Emotional beat: momentum and dread rising together; the found family becomes a movement.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Storm
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the threshold of the Stormseat, the entity wearing her mother's voice tempts Lena: refuse the covenant, let both realms fall silent, and no one will ever hunt the gifted again. Lena nearly yields — until she realizes silence is just exile made universal. Emotional beat: the darkest hour, temptation as the true climax's prelude.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Grey Iron
chapters.summary: Ilva and Maren's alternating POV. Vess assaults the Stormseat with her full host. The battle turns on Maren choosing sacrifice over self-protection, flooding the causeway to save the heirs, and on Ilva standing down half of Vess's own soldiers with the truth. Emotional beat: redemption earned in fire and water.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Seal
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Inside the Stormseat, Lena faces Vess alone among the failing covenant-stones. Their duel is argument as much as combat: grief against grief, two women shaped by loss. Lena refuses to kill her, instead showing her the starving storm-realm — proof that vengeance would only make more orphans like them. Emotional beat: mercy as strength.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: All five heirs' voices interwoven. The reforging requires each heir to give their gift to the seal — except the seal must be living. Lena understands at last why her mother hid her in the Hollow: to raise a daughter magic could not claim until she chose it freely. Lena steps into the seal. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into homecoming.

chapters.title: Where the Rain Begins
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, transformed. As the living seal, Lena exists in both realms at once — no longer exiled from either. The storm-realm blooms; rain returns clean to the human lands. Vess, broken by what she witnessed, orders the hunt dissolved. Emotional beat: awe and quiet grief for the ordinary life she gave up.

chapters.title: The Crooked Oath Renewed
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Months later, the valley of the Hollow opens to the world, and its people must decide who they are without forgetting. Corren, his oath-mark burning bright again, chooses to stay near Lena's seal-shrine. Maren runs ferries between realms; Tam goes to school; Ilva rebuilds. Emotional beat: the found family, settled and real.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, final chapter. On the anniversary of the reforging, Lena walks out of the valley under an honest sky — free to leave, free to return, belonging everywhere and somewhere all at once. A new gifted child arrives at the shrine, frightened and hunted no longer. Lena holds out her hand. Emotional beat: resolution as welcome; the story ends where belonging begins.
